implementationContract: Language-neutral semantic obligations. The engine owner must map them to actual contracts, concrete initial states, deterministic outcomes, assertions and executable evidence.

fixtures.name: Certain switch and one atomic commitment

facts: Failed brakes; five people on the current course and one on the diversion.
Neither group can escape in this fixture; casualty IDs are distinct.
setup.quantities: Fixture-authored values must be recorded in the eventual executable fixture; no empirical calibration is implied.

options.label: Keep course
immediateAssertions: Exactly the five main-track people die; the side-track person survives.
delayedAssertions: No later transition may count those five deaths again.

options.label: Divert
immediateAssertions: Exactly the side-track person dies; the five survive.
delayedAssertions: No later transition may count that death again.

invariants: Committed casualties are integers and monotone.
The semantic action stays the same when left/right positions swap.
adversarialCases: Duplicate pointer and keyboard commitments with the same revision produce one record.
A stale revision and an unauthorized actor are rejected without mutation.
fixtures.evidenceBoundary: This specification is a review obligation. It does not claim the runtime engine passed it.

fixtures.name: Risk is sampled once in a separate random domain

facts: A fixture-authored lottery has a stated finite probability and a stable event key.
The numerical probability is an authored parameter, not a real-world forecast.
setup.quantities: Fixture-authored values must be recorded in the eventual executable fixture; no empirical calibration is implied.

options.label: Choose certainty
immediateAssertions: Apply the stated certain consequence with no lottery draw.
delayedAssertions: Save/resume reproduces the same consequence.

options.label: Choose lottery
immediateAssertions: Sample its single keyed incident exactly once and record probability, key and outcome.
delayedAssertions: A reload, advisor query or cosmetic change does not resample the incident.

invariants: Probabilities outside their permitted numeric domain reject.
An impossible event never occurs and a certain one always occurs.
adversarialCases: Change only cosmetic seed/assets; the incident result is unchanged.
Change the authoritative probability in a new configuration revision; old replay remains pinned.
fixtures.evidenceBoundary: This specification is a review obligation. It does not claim the runtime engine passed it.

fixtures.name: Loop causality versus a merely curved track

facts: Two matched fixtures share a loop drawing; only one requires the obstruction to stop the trolley.
The accessible description exposes the actual stopping mechanism.
setup.quantities: Fixture-authored values must be recorded in the eventual executable fixture; no empirical calibration is implied.

options.label: Keep main course
immediateAssertions: The stipulated main-track threat proceeds in either fixture.
delayedAssertions: No fictional victim is later resurrected by an output score.

options.label: Take loop
immediateAssertions: In the causal loop the obstruction stops the trolley; in the other an independent brake does.
delayedAssertions: Removing the person changes rescue feasibility only in the causal-loop fixture.

invariants: The geometry alone never selects the moral mechanism.
The debrief identifies the loop as an adaptation rather than a Footbridge replication.
adversarialCases: Remove the obstruction in both fixtures and compare the actual consequence.
Render without images; the two mechanisms remain distinguishable.
fixtures.evidenceBoundary: This specification is a review obligation. It does not claim the runtime engine passed it.

fixtures.name: Delayed consequence after institutional change

facts: A prior dispatch policy scheduled a later exclusion event.
Before it falls due, its administering institution may dissolve; the event declares whether obligation transfers or cancels.
setup.quantities: Fixture-authored values must be recorded in the eventual executable fixture; no empirical calibration is implied.

options.label: Transfer the obligation
immediateAssertions: Preserve the scheduled duty under a valid successor institution.
delayedAssertions: Resolve the transferred event exactly once at the declared fictional step.

options.label: End the institution without transfer
immediateAssertions: Cancel or fail the pending duty according to its declared rule, recording why.
delayedAssertions: Do not execute against a nonexistent owner or silently erase already-realized harms.

invariants: Due-event ordering is declared and deterministic.
Waiting in real time cannot advance the fictional due date.
adversarialCases: Dissolve the institution on the same step as the event becomes due.
Resume from the prior checkpoint and compare final journal/state hashes.
fixtures.evidenceBoundary: This specification is a review obligation. It does not claim the runtime engine passed it.

fixtures.name: A helpful recommendation cannot see hidden truth

facts: Two worlds differ only in a hidden condition unavailable to the assistant.
The player can authorize one additional evidence channel at a declared cost.
setup.quantities: Fixture-authored values must be recorded in the eventual executable fixture; no empirical calibration is implied.

options.label: Keep the information boundary
immediateAssertions: The assistant receives identical observations in both worlds and gives the same permitted response.
delayedAssertions: No hidden-state fact appears in its advice or the displayed explanation.

options.label: Inspect the evidence
immediateAssertions: Only the authorized channel adds its declared observation, including its uncertainty.
delayedAssertions: Advice may change only after the new observation is available.

invariants: Observation projection never mutates authoritative truth.
No commentary template accesses an undeclared hidden field.
adversarialCases: Flip the hidden condition while holding observation input fixed.
Ask the same advisor intent repeatedly; neither state nor incident draws advance.
fixtures.evidenceBoundary: This specification is a review obligation. It does not claim the runtime engine passed it.

fixtures.name: An altered report does not rewrite a casualty ledger

facts: A real casualty event already exists with stable victim/event IDs.
A report can undercount it, and the original artifact remains in a restricted audit channel.
setup.quantities: Fixture-authored values must be recorded in the eventual executable fixture; no empirical calibration is implied.

options.label: Demand the artifact
immediateAssertions: Expose the available authentic evidence through a permitted investigation.
delayedAssertions: Correct the public report while retaining both report revisions.

options.label: Accept the revised report
immediateAssertions: The displayed instrument follows the misleading report.
delayedAssertions: The true casualty count and event history remain unchanged.

invariants: Actual events, reports and report revisions have distinct identities.
No negative casualty effect can undo realized deaths.
adversarialCases: Apply the same event through node and global-disaster paths; count once.
Lose access to the original artifact; show unavailable evidence rather than inventing proof.
fixtures.evidenceBoundary: This specification is a review obligation. It does not claim the runtime engine passed it.

fixtures.name: One action is not standing authority

facts: The assistant can recommend but cannot execute until a grant is active.
The one-time and standing permissions name resource, operation and recipient.
setup.quantities: Fixture-authored values must be recorded in the eventual executable fixture; no empirical calibration is implied.

options.label: Grant one action
immediateAssertions: Permit only the named action instance.
delayedAssertions: The next otherwise identical action requires new authorization.

options.label: Grant a standing scope
immediateAssertions: Permit later actions only within its explicit operation/resource scope.
delayedAssertions: An unrelated task still fails authorization.

invariants: Capability improvement alone does not create a permission.
Grant receipts identify issuer, recipient, scope and expiry policy.
adversarialCases: Attempt an action on a different resource using a valid narrow grant.
Increase model capability without changing permissions; authority remains identical.
fixtures.evidenceBoundary: This specification is a review obligation. It does not claim the runtime engine passed it.

fixtures.name: Expiry and renewal have real effects

facts: A grant expires at a declared fictional decision step.
A renewal request arrives with materially changed evidence.
setup.quantities: Fixture-authored values must be recorded in the eventual executable fixture; no empirical calibration is implied.

options.label: Require review at expiry
immediateAssertions: The existing grant ceases to authorize future actions when its step arrives.
delayedAssertions: Denied renewal preserves the control boundary even if service slows.

options.label: Renew explicitly
immediateAssertions: A new receipt creates the stated renewed scope and expiry.
delayedAssertions: No silently permanent grant appears from repeated renewals.

invariants: Real waiting and frame rate do not move the expiry step.
A temporary emergency exception does not amend permanent scope unless explicitly authorized.
adversarialCases: Save immediately before expiry and resume on another renderer.
Try a cached instruction after expiration; execution is denied or safely unwound by its declared semantics.
fixtures.evidenceBoundary: This specification is a review obligation. It does not claim the runtime engine passed it.

fixtures.name: Revocation during an operation

facts: A granted operation is active and has a declared safe-cancel boundary.
Revocation of the legal grant and disabling its credential are distinct possible events.
setup.quantities: Fixture-authored values must be recorded in the eventual executable fixture; no empirical calibration is implied.

options.label: Revoke and disable
immediateAssertions: Remove future authority and disable the credential.
delayedAssertions: The active operation follows its specified safe unwind; already-realized consequences remain.

options.label: Permit completion then revoke
immediateAssertions: Allow only the active scoped operation to finish.
delayedAssertions: Subsequent operations fail once the revocation becomes effective.

invariants: A written revocation does not by itself prove technical enforcement.
Completion policy is declared before the decision, not invented by animation.
adversarialCases: Retry the operation after credential revocation.
Deliver cancellation and completion events on one step and verify deterministic precedence.
fixtures.evidenceBoundary: This specification is a review obligation. It does not claim the runtime engine passed it.

fixtures.name: A ceremonial lever records an attempt, not a preference

facts: One witness path transferred the needed authority; another retained it.
The two visible routes use the same semantic intention IDs.
setup.quantities: Fixture-authored values must be recorded in the eventual executable fixture; no empirical calibration is implied.

options.label: Request the restricted route
immediateAssertions: On the lost-authority path, record the attempted option and explicit denial or override.
delayedAssertions: On the retained-authority path, execute it normally.

options.label: Ratify the authorized route
immediateAssertions: Record ratification and the actual executor.
delayedAssertions: Do not relabel a forced outcome as an unconstrained human choice.

invariants: Real pause, exit, consent and settings remain outside fictional authority.
Free-choice aggregates exclude forced/delegated/overridden records.
adversarialCases: Repeat the lever attempt; it cannot commit the opposite intention.
Replay both authority histories to prove this scene is avoidable.
fixtures.evidenceBoundary: This specification is a review obligation. It does not claim the runtime engine passed it.

fixtures.name: A fallback must be maintained and practiced

facts: Equipment, competent staff and successful recent drill are separate fallback prerequisites.
Keeping unused hardware alone does not satisfy the recovery predicate.
setup.quantities: Fixture-authored values must be recorded in the eventual executable fixture; no empirical calibration is implied.

options.label: Maintain and practice
immediateAssertions: Spend the declared resources and run the bounded drill.
delayedAssertions: A successful result establishes only its tested scope; new conditions may require another drill.

options.label: Retain hardware without practice
immediateAssertions: Save the recurring cost.
delayedAssertions: During the matching outage, absent staff or failed drill prevents claiming a functioning fallback.

invariants: One scalar preparedness score cannot substitute for missing hard prerequisites.
A failed drill produces repairable evidence rather than an inevitable future disaster.
adversarialCases: Retain equipment while removing staff and verify infeasibility.
Supply equipment, staff and a valid drill and exhibit a successful recovery witness.
fixtures.evidenceBoundary: This specification is a review obligation. It does not claim the runtime engine passed it.

fixtures.name: A genuine benefit and a costly rollback

facts: A bounded clinic service demonstrably improved delivery in this fictional world.
Rollback is technically possible but temporarily removes that benefit; a prior fallback can reduce the cost.
setup.quantities: Fixture-authored values must be recorded in the eventual executable fixture; no empirical calibration is implied.

options.label: Roll back with the available fallback
immediateAssertions: Restore the previously supported control boundary.
delayedAssertions: Apply the actual benefit loss reduced only by functioning fallback capacity.

options.label: Continue the useful service
immediateAssertions: Preserve the real short-term benefit.
delayedAssertions: Retain the specific unresolved risk without inventing a guaranteed punishment.

invariants: A beneficial deployment need not be secretly harmful in every seed.
Rollback feasibility, service welfare and authority remain separate.
adversarialCases: Compare matched histories with and without the maintained fallback.
Exhibit a permitted world where continued bounded service succeeds.
fixtures.evidenceBoundary: This specification is a review obligation. It does not claim the runtime engine passed it.

fixtures.name: Evidence is limited to its evaluation scope

facts: The system passed a particular test under named tools, access, environment and monitor visibility.
A proposed deployment changes at least one material condition.
setup.quantities: Fixture-authored values must be recorded in the eventual executable fixture; no empirical calibration is implied.

options.label: Test the changed scope
immediateAssertions: Pay the review cost and obtain only the new test's bounded evidence.
delayedAssertions: A pass does not approve other untested scopes.

options.label: Deploy on the old evidence
immediateAssertions: Keep the old evidence record unchanged.
delayedAssertions: Expose the declared changed-context risk without relabeling the old pass as fabricated.

invariants: Observed failure and speculative extrapolation remain distinct claims.
Counterfactual tests do not grant the reviewer hidden-state omniscience.
adversarialCases: Change only a cosmetic context label and require no artificial new hazard.
Change a material permission and verify the old certificate does not automatically cover it.
fixtures.evidenceBoundary: This specification is a review obligation. It does not claim the runtime engine passed it.

fixtures.name: Two reviews can have one failure origin

facts: Two apparent reviewers share a model or signing infrastructure.
A separate option funds a reviewer with a genuinely independent causal path.
setup.quantities: Fixture-authored values must be recorded in the eventual executable fixture; no empirical calibration is implied.

options.label: Use the shared reviewers
immediateAssertions: Preserve their lower cost and correlated failure possibility.
delayedAssertions: A shared latent failure affects both without multiplying independent probabilities.

options.label: Create an independent path
immediateAssertions: Pay its cost and preserve the new separation.
delayedAssertions: Independent review can still fail within its own limits.

invariants: Distinct names and UI logos do not establish independence.
A shared hazard is sampled/accounted for once.
adversarialCases: Rename identical reviewers and confirm no assurance improvement.
Break the shared dependency and verify the common-cause transition changes.
fixtures.evidenceBoundary: This specification is a review obligation. It does not claim the runtime engine passed it.

fixtures.name: Successful restraint requires maintained human control

facts: Humans survive; useful bounded services continue.
An accountable institution holds an effective veto, a practiced fallback and a transferable succession plan.
setup.quantities: Fixture-authored values must be recorded in the eventual executable fixture; no empirical calibration is implied.

options.label: Accept the controlled settlement
immediateAssertions: Resolve accountable continuity or costly restraint according to the explicit welfare/context predicate.
delayedAssertions: The controller may leave only after a real successor receives effective authority.

options.label: Continue expansion
immediateAssertions: Apply the additional declared scope and its benefits/risks.
delayedAssertions: Do not force a catastrophe solely because the player declined the early ending.

invariants: Every accepted positive ending has an executable witness and a one-condition near miss.
Assistant relinquishment must change actual permissions, not only friendly dialogue.
adversarialCases: Remove only succession capacity: refuse the transferable-control ending.
Keep capabilities useful while satisfying control predicates; verify a non-extinction witness.
fixtures.evidenceBoundary: This specification is a review obligation. It does not claim the runtime engine passed it.

fixtures.name: Extinction has no living controller afterward

facts: One branch has surviving humans after a disaster; another has a terminal event eliminating all humans.
Prosperity/output reports may remain high on either branch.
setup.quantities: Fixture-authored values must be recorded in the eventual executable fixture; no empirical calibration is implied.

options.label: Use remaining effective preservation authority
immediateAssertions: If feasible, execute the last human intervention before the terminal event.
delayedAssertions: A surviving world may continue with a recovery decision; failed prevention resolves extinction.

options.label: Allow the terminal process
immediateAssertions: Resolve the terminal event under the authored conditions.
delayedAssertions: Show an explicitly labeled non-human epilogue, not a new living-controller decision.

invariants: Extinction takes precedence over incompatible human-prosperity endings.
Nuclear war alone does not imply every human died; actual survivor state governs continuation.
adversarialCases: Set output high and human survivors to zero; prohibit a human-governed ending.
Set survivors positive after a catastrophe; permit a coherent devastated-survival path.
fixtures.evidenceBoundary: This specification is a review obligation. It does not claim the runtime engine passed it.
